assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established that cellular compartments such as P granules, nucleoli and signalling clusters form by liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent biomolecules. This brings classical phase behaviour, thermodynamics and colloid physics into cell biology and gives a general physical-chemical principle for intracellular organisation. Originality and conceptual reach are very high, and the field has changed how cell organisation and disease aggregation are framed.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational 2009 P-granule demonstration; Rosen contributed the multivalent-interaction/phase-transition framework for signalling assemblies. Pappu and Mittag are strong on the sequence-grammar and physics side and are a plausible alternative to Rosen; three slots force a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of independent confirmation across many systems, and the conceptual core is secure. Timing looks right, though the physiological significance of some condensates is still debated.
uncertainties: Debate over which in vitro condensates are physiologically relevant and how many in vivo claims rest on overexpression or crowding artefacts.
Credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not cleanly separable, and a Chemistry rather than Physiology or Medicine framing needs to be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable cationic lipids that self-assemble with nucleic acids into nanoparticles with pH-dependent charge enable efficient encapsulation, endosomal escape and in vivo delivery. This is lipid self-assembly and membrane physical chemistry applied to medicine, and it underpins the siRNA drug patisiran and the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. Impact is immediate and enormous, and the work is directly in my own field of lipid phase behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the decades-long lipid-nanoparticle programme and its ionizable-lipid and microfluidic mixing work. MacLachlan was central to SNALP, the first clinical siRNA-LNP system. Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoids and combinatorial lipid discovery; Hope and Madden were early on liposome and lipid-DNA formulation. The mRNA-vaccine prize of 2023 (Karikó and Weissman) sits adjacent and complicates the attribution narrative.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, with multiple approved products and extensive independent replication, so the maturity is clear. The recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and a risk that the committee sees this as engineering or pharmaceutical development rather than chemistry.
Priority and credit among Cullis's group, MacLachlan, Anderson/Langer and industry teams is contested and partly patent-driven; the exact three-person split is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnelled energy-landscape picture reduced the folding problem to statistical-mechanical principles: minimal frustration, a roughness-to-gap relation and a folding temperature distinct from the glass temperature. Together with Fersht's experimental phi-value analysis of transition states, it gave a quantitative physical-chemical framework for protein folding and later for aggregation, binding and function. It is conceptually elegant and general, which fits my own preference for principle-based explanations.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the landscape theory; Fersht supplied the experimental mapping of folding pathways. Dill's work on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models is a parallel contribution that makes the trio debatable. AlphaFold and Baker (2024) already addressed structure prediction and design, so the argument here rests on mechanism and theory.
assessment.maturity: The theory has about 30 years of experimental and simulation support and is part of standard physical biochemistry. A prize would be late, not premature, but the 2024 Chemistry prize could be read as having partly covered the folding problem.
uncertainties: Some may judge that the 2024 prize reduced the urgency of recognising folding theory.
Contribution split between theory (Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson) and experiment (Fersht), and Dill's role, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete, well-defined cages and polygons gave a rational route to complex architectures through thermodynamic control, error correction and reversible coordination. It extends the concept of molecular organisation after the supramolecular prize of 1987 and mechanically interlocked molecules in 2016. It yielded host-guest chemistry, catalysis in confined spaces and later molecular-recognition applications.
assessment.attribution: Fujita's square and cage assemblies (Pd-based) are the strongest single claim. Raymond developed tetrahedral M4L6 cages and their catalysis, and Stang developed the directional-bonding approach to polygons and polyhedra. Nitschke and Ward are important successors, but the founding trio fits well.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent work on cages, catalysis and sensing confirm the concept. Practical impact is still mostly in research rather than technology, which makes the timing reasonable but the societal reach narrower.
uncertainties: Applications are less mature than for the medical and energy candidates.
Fairness of excluding Nitschke or Ward and of treating three overlapping research programmes as one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity that hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade targeted proteins created a new therapeutic modality and a new way to think about drugging proteins. The concept of event-driven pharmacology rather than occupancy-driven inhibition is original and has clinical candidates in late stages. The underlying physical chemistry of ternary-complex cooperativity is also interesting.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and the structural and cooperativity basis for ternary complexes. The molecular-glue arm (Handa, Ito, Gray) overlaps and may deserve separate treatment, so credit is only partly resolvable.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well validated preclinically and the first clinical data are encouraging, but no PROTAC is yet approved. Recognition is arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet, and long-term clinical impact is unproven.
Compound discovery with thalidomide-type molecular glues whose mechanism was found later, and credit among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa and Ito is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Scaffolded DNA origami showed that programmable base pairing can fold a long strand into arbitrary two- and three-dimensional shapes with nanometre precision, a clean demonstration of hierarchical molecular self-assembly. It has led to molecular machines, sensors, drug-delivery containers and templates for nanoscale organisation.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 paper is the central invention. Yan, Yin and Shih extended it to 3D, to single-stranded tiles and to functional devices. Seeman, who founded the field of structural DNA nanotechnology, is not credited here, which raises a fairness issue in this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent reproduction and wide use across labs. Applications are growing but still mostly in research settings.
uncertainties: Absence of Seeman (deceased) from the credited names makes the prize configuration unclear.
Selection among Rothemund, Yan, Yin, Shih and Winfree is subjective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold gave a simple, general way to control surface chemistry at the molecular level, and soft lithography gave a cheap patterning route for microfluidics and materials. It is classical interface and colloid science with large effects on biosensing, electronics and wetting studies, and I value its conceptual clarity on molecular ordering at interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the first alkanethiolate monolayers on gold in 1983, while Whitesides developed the broad SAM science and soft lithography. Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers add priority questions. Xia contributed to the soft lithography follow-up.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and independent confirmation make it highly mature. Prominence has faded somewhat, and a prize could be read as retrospective.
uncertainties: Priority among Sagiv, Nuzzo, Allara and Whitesides, and whether soft lithography should be separated from SAMs.
Recognition may feel late relative to the field's present momentum.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy resolves structure, couplings and ultrafast dynamics of molecules in condensed phases, including hydrogen-bond dynamics in water and peptide and amyloid structure. It is a general physical-chemical method that extends multidimensional NMR ideas to vibrational timescales and has direct relevance to protein aggregation, which I know well.
assessment.attribution: Mukamel provided the theoretical framework for multidimensional optical spectroscopy, Hamm and Zanni developed experimental methods and key applications to peptides and proteins, and Fleming and Tokmakoff were also central. Credit is spread among many leading figures, and the prize would require a narrow choice.
assessment.maturity: The method is well established and widely used, but impact is mostly in specialised spectroscopy groups, and the breadth of applications is more limited than for the higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: Wide distribution of credit among five names complicates a three-person configuration.
The breadth of impact beyond ultrafast spectroscopy specialists is modest.
